items.title: Show Me The Body Bring The Real Freak Shit To Town
items.summary: It happens about once a year: Show Me The Body announce a huge North American tour with an absolutely baffling array of opening acts. Every time I open the email, I say "whoa" out loud. It never fails. SMTB usually pick their openers from the hardcore underground, but not always. The acts on the bill almost never sound much of anything like each other, but they always put on intense, aggressive live shows, and I always walk out feeling like I've had a great Sheetz combo meal of things that really shouldn't make sense together — some cheese curds, a breakfast burrito, maybe some sour Skittles.

items.title: Piero Umiliani :: Il Corpo
items.summary: Piero Umiliani’s Il Corpo is the sound of something beautiful beginning to sour. Released in 1974, the soundtrack finds the Italian composer in familiar aesthetic territory, where jazz, funk, psychedelia and library music bleed into one another: Hammond organ, wah guitar, languid strings and exotic percussion. Sunny music for shady people, it embodies the anything-goes spirit of Italian library music, spinning a parallel film from grooves, fuzz and atmosphere. The post Piero Umiliani :: Il Corpo first appeared on Aquarium Drunkard .
